study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized controlled trial
exposure: Previous pregnancy loss before 20 weeks of gestation
Perinatal death or severe neonatal complications
outcome: Self-reported perceived control during childbirth (Labor Agentry Scale score)
cohort: 5,750 low-risk nulliparous individuals who experienced labor and completed the Labor Agentry Scale questionnaire.
finding: Unemployment, lack of private health insurance, Asian race, Hispanic ethnicity, smoking, operative delivery, and greater labor pain were associated with lower self-reported perceived control during labor in low-risk nulliparous individuals.
mod_finding: Operative vaginal or cesarean delivery was associated with significantly lower perceived control during labor compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
